text: You know, if you are a country and you’re trying to gain the support of another country, then you want to do everything you can that they would act in a cooperative fashion.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: When you announce that you’re going to launch an attack into another country, it’s pretty obvious that you have the effect that it had in Pakistan: It turns public opinion against us.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, let me just go back with you very briefly.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We drove the Russians out with — the Afghan freedom fighters drove the Russians out of Afghanistan, and then we made a most serious mistake.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We washed our hands of Afghanistan.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The Taliban came back in, Al Qaida, we then had the situation that required us to conduct the Afghan war.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, our relations with Pakistan are critical, because the border areas are being used as safe havens by the Taliban and Al Qaida and other extremist organizations, and we have to get their support.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, General Petraeus had a strategy, the same strategy — very, very different, because of the conditions and the situation — but the same fundamental strategy that succeeded in Iraq.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And that is to get the support of the people.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We need to help the Pakistani government go into Waziristan, where I visited, a very rough country, and — and get the support of the people, and get them to work with us and turn against the cruel Taliban and others.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And by working and coordinating our efforts together, not threatening to attack them, but working with them, and where necessary use force, but talk softly, but carry a big stick.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Tom, just a…

speaker: BROKAW
text: Senator McCain…

speaker: OBAMA
text: … just a quick follow-up on this.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: If we’re going to have follow-ups, then I will want follow-ups, as well.

speaker: BROKAW
text: No, I know.

speaker: BROKAW
text: So but I think we get at it…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’d be fine with me.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’d be fine with me.

speaker: BROKAW
text: … if I can, with this question.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Then let’s have one.

speaker: BROKAW
text: All right, let’s have a follow-up.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’d be fine with me.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Just — just — just a quick follow-up, because I think — I think this is important.

speaker: BROKAW
text: I’m just the hired help here, so, I mean…

speaker: OBAMA
text: You’re doing a great job, Tom.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Look, I — I want to be very clear about what I said.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Nobody called for the invasion of Pakistan.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Senator McCain continues to repeat this.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What I said was the same thing that the audience here today heard me say, which is, if Pakistan is unable or unwilling to hunt down bin Laden and take him out, then we should.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, that I think has to be our policy, because they are threatening to kill more Americans.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, Senator McCain suggests that somehow, you know, I’m green behind the ears and, you know, I’m just spouting off, and he’s somber and responsible.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Thank you very much.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Senator McCain, this is the guy who sang, “Bomb, bomb, bomb Iran,” who called for the annihilation of North Korea.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That I don’t think is an example of “speaking softly.

speaker: OBAMA
text: ” This is the person who, after we had — we hadn’t even finished Afghanistan, where he said, “Next up, Baghdad.

speaker: OBAMA
text: ” So I agree that we have to speak responsibly and we have to act responsibly.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And the reason Pakistan — the popular opinion of America had diminished in Pakistan was because we were supporting a dictator, Musharraf, had given him $10 billion over seven years, and he had suspended civil liberties.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We were not promoting democracy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: This is the kind of policies that ultimately end up undermining our ability to fight the war on terrorism, and it will change when I’m president.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And, Tom, if — if we’re going to go back and forth, I then — I’d like to have equal time to go — to respond to…

speaker: BROKAW
text: Yes, you get the…

speaker: MCCAIN
text: … to — to — to…

speaker: BROKAW
text: … last word here, and then we have to move on.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Not true.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Not true.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I have, obviously, supported those efforts that the United States had to go in militarily and I have opposed that I didn’t think so.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I understand what it’s like to send young American’s in harm’s way.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I say — I was joking with a veteran — I hate to even go into this.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I was joking with an old veteran friend, who joked with me, about Iran.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But the point is that I know how to handle these crises.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And Senator Obama, by saying that he would attack Pakistan, look at the context of his words.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’ll get Osama bin Laden, my friends.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’ll get him.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I know how to get him.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I’ll get him no matter what and I know how to do it.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But I’m not going to telegraph my punches, which is what Senator Obama did.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I’m going to act responsibly, as I have acted responsibly throughout my military career and throughout my career in the United States Senate.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And we have fundamental disagreements about the use of military power and how you do it, and you just saw it in response to previous questions.

text: Can I get a quick response from the two of you about developments in Afghanistan this week?

speaker: BROKAW
text: The senior British military commander, who is now leading there for a second tour, and their senior diplomatic presence there, Sherard Cowper-Coles, who is well known as an expert in the area, both have said that we’re failing in Afghanistan.

speaker: BROKAW
text: The commander said we cannot win there.

speaker: BROKAW
text: We’ve got to get it down to a low level insurgency, let the Afghans take it over.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Cowper-Coles said what we need is an acceptable dictator.

speaker: BROKAW
text: If either of you becomes president, as one of you will, how do you reorganize Afghanistan’s strategy or do you?

speaker: BROKAW
text: Briefly, if you can.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I’ll be very brief.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We are going to have to make the Iraqi government start taking more responsibility, withdraw our troops in a responsible way over time, because we’re going to have to put some additional troops in Afghanistan.

speaker: OBAMA
text: General McKiernan, the commander in Afghanistan right now, is desperate for more help, because our bases and outposts are now targets for more aggressive Afghan — Taliban offenses.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’re also going to have to work with the Karzai government, and when I met with President Karzai, I was very clear that, “You are going to have to do better by your people in order for us to gain the popular support that’s necessary.

speaker: OBAMA
text: ” I don’t think he has to be a dictator.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we want a democracy in Afghanistan.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But we have to have a government that is responsive to the Afghan people, and, frankly, it’s just not responsive right now.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Senator McCain, briefly.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: General Petraeus has just taken over a position of responsibility, where he has the command and will really set the tone for the strategy and tactics that are used.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I’ve had conversations with him.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It is the same overall strategy.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Of course, we have to do some things tactically, some of which Senator Obama is correct on.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We have to double the size of the Afghan army.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We have to have a streamlined NATO command structure.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We have to do a lot of things.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We have to work much more closely with the Pakistanis.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But most importantly, we have to have the same strategy, which Senator Obama said wouldn’t work, couldn’t work, still fails to admit that he was wrong about Iraq.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He still will not admit that he was wrong about the strategy of the surge in Iraq, and that’s the same kind of strategy of go out and secure and hold and allow people to live normal lives.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And once they feel secure, then they lead normal, social, economic, political lives, the same thing that’s happening in Iraq today.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So I have confidence that General Petraeus, working with the Pakistanis, working with the Afghans, doing the same job that he did in Iraq, will again.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We will succeed and we will bring our troops home with honor and victory and not in defeat.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Senator McCain, this question is for you from the Internet.

speaker: BROKAW
text: It’s from Alden in Hewitt, Texas.

speaker: BROKAW
text: How can we apply pressure to Russia for humanitarian issues in an effective manner without starting another Cold War?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: First of all, as I say, I don’t think that — we’re not going to have another Cold War with Russia.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But have no doubt that Russia’s behavior is certainly outside the norms of behavior that we would expect for nations which are very wealthy, as Russia has become, because of their petro dollars.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, long ago, I warned about Vladimir Putin.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I said I looked into his eyes and saw three letters, a K, a G and a B.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He has surrounded himself with former KGB apparatchiks.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: He has gradually repressed most of the liberties that we would expect for nations to observe, and he has exhibited most aggressive behavior, obviously, in Georgia.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I said before, watch Ukraine.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Ukraine, right now, is in the sights of Vladimir Putin, those that want to reassemble the old Soviet Union.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’ve got to show moral support for Georgia.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’ve got to show moral support for Ukraine.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We’ve got to advocate for their membership in NATO.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: We have to make the Russians understand that there are penalties for these this kind of behavior, this kind of naked aggression into Georgia, a tiny country and a tiny democracy.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And so, of course we want to bring international pressures to bear on Russia in hopes that that will modify and eventually change their behavior.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, the G-8 is one of those, but there are many others.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But the Russians must understand that these kinds of actions and activities are not acceptable and hopefully we will use the leverage, economic, diplomatic and others united with our allies, with our allies and friends in Europe who are equally disturbed as we are about their recent behaviors.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Senator Obama.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It will not be a re-ignition of the Cold War, but Russia is a challenge.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Senator Obama?

speaker: BROKAW
text: We’re winding down, so if we can keep track of the time.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, the resurgence of Russia is one of the central issues that we’re going to have to deal with in the next presidency.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And for the most part I agree with Senator McCain on many of the steps that have to be taken.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But we can’t just provide moral support.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to provide moral support to the Poles and Estonia and Latvia and all of the nations that were former Soviet satellites.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But we’ve also got to provide them with financial and concrete assistance to help rebuild their economies.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Georgia in particular is now on the brink of enormous economic challenges.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And some say that that’s what Putin intended in the first place.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The other thing we have to do, though, is we’ve got to see around the corners.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to anticipate some of these problems ahead of time.

speaker: OBAMA
text: You know, back in April, I put out a statement saying that the situation in Georgia was unsustainable because you had Russian peacekeepers in these territories that were under dispute.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And you knew that if the Russians themselves were trying to obtain some of these territories or push back against Georgia, that that was not a stable situation.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So part of the job of the next commander-in-chief, in keeping all of you safe, is making sure that we can see some of the 21st Century challenges and anticipate them before they happen.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We haven’t been doing enough of that.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We tend to be reactive.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s what we’ve been doing over the last eight years and that has actually made us more safe.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s part of what happened in Afghanistan, where we rushed into Iraq and Senator McCain and President Bush suggested that it wasn’t that important to catch bin Laden right now and that we could muddle through, and that has cost us dearly.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to be much more strategic if we’re going to be able to deal with all of the challenges that we face out there.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And one last point I want to make about Russia.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Energy is going to be key in dealing with Russia.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we can reduce our energy consumption, that reduces the amount of petro dollars that they have to make mischief around the world.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That will strengthen us and weaken them when it comes to issues like Georgia.

speaker: BROKAW
text: This requires only a yes or a no.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Ronald Reagan famously said that the Soviet Union was the evil empire.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Do you think that Russia under Vladimir Putin is an evil empire?

speaker: OBAMA
text: I think they’ve engaged in an evil behavior and I think that it is important that we understand they’re not the old Soviet Union but they still have nationalist impulses that I think are very dangerous.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Senator McCain?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Maybe.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Maybe.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Depends on how we respond to Russia and it depends on a lot of things.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: If I say yes, then that means that we’re reigniting the old Cold War.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: If I say no, it ignores their behavior.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Obviously energy is going to be a big, big factor.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And Georgia and Ukraine are both major gateways of energy into Europe.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And that’s one of the reasons why it’s in our interest.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But the Russians, I think we can deal with them but they’ve got to understand that they’re facing a very firm and determined United States of America that will defend our interests and that of other countries in the world.

speaker: BROKAW
text: All right.

speaker: BROKAW
text: We’re going to try to get in two more questions, if we can.

speaker: BROKAW
text: So we have to move along.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Over in section A, Terry Chary — do I have that right, Terry?

speaker: BROKAW
text: QUESTION: Senator, as a retired Navy chief, my thoughts are often with those who serve our country.

speaker: BROKAW
text: I know both candidates, both of you, expressed support for Israel.

speaker: QUESTION
text: If, despite your best diplomatic efforts, Iran attacks Israel, would you be willing to commit U.

speaker: QUESTION
text: troops in support and defense of Israel?

speaker: QUESTION
text: Or would you wait on approval from the U.

speaker: QUESTION
text: Security Council?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, thank you, Terry .

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And thank you for your service to the country.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I want to say, everything I ever learned about leadership I learned from a chief petty officer.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I thank you, and I thank you, my friend.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Thanks for serving.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Let — let — let me say that we obviously would not wait for the United Nations Security Council.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I think the realities are that both Russia and China would probably pose significant obstacles.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And our challenge right now is the Iranians continue on the path to acquiring nuclear weapons, and it’s a great threat.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s not just a threat — threat to the state of Israel.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s a threat to the stability of the entire Middle East.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: If Iran acquires nuclear weapons, all the other countries will acquire them, too.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The tensions will be ratcheted up.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: What would you do if you were the Israelis and the president of a country says that they are — they are determined to wipe you off the map, calls your country a stinking corpse?

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Now, Senator Obama without precondition wants to sit down and negotiate with them, without preconditions.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s what he stated, again, a matter of record.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I want to make sure that the Iranians are put enough — that we put enough pressure on the Iranians by joining with our allies, imposing significant, tough sanctions to modify their behavior.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I think we can do that.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I think, joining with our allies and friends in a league of democracies, that we can effectively abridge their behavior, and hopefully they would abandon this quest that they are on for nuclear weapons.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But, at the end of the day, my friend, I have to tell you again, and you know what it’s like to serve, and you know what it’s like to sacrifice, but we can never allow a second Holocaust to take place.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Senator Obama?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, Terry, first of all, we honor your service, and we’re grateful for it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We cannot allow Iran to get a nuclear weapon.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It would be a game-changer in the region.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Not only would it threaten Israel, our strongest ally in the region and one of our strongest allies in the world, but it would also create a possibility of nuclear weapons falling into the hands of terrorists.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And so it’s unacceptable.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I will do everything that’s required to prevent it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we will never take military options off the table.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And it is important that we don’t provide veto power to the United Nations or anyone else in acting in our interests.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It is important, though, for us to use all the tools at our disposal to prevent the scenario where we’ve got to make those kinds of choices.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And that’s why I have consistently said that, if we can work more effectively with other countries diplomatically to tighten sanctions on Iran, if we can reduce our energy consumption through alternative energy, so that Iran has less money, if we can impose the kinds of sanctions that, say, for example, Iran right now imports gasoline, even though it’s an oil-producer, because its oil infrastructure has broken down, if we can prevent them from importing the gasoline that they need and the refined petroleum products, that starts changing their cost-benefit analysis.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That starts putting the squeeze on them.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, it is true, though, that I believe that we should have direct talks — not just with our friends, but also with our enemies — to deliver a tough, direct message to Iran that, if you don’t change your behavior, then there will be dire consequences.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If you do change your behavior, then it is possible for you to re-join the community of nations.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, it may not work.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But one of the things we’ve learned is, is that when we take that approach, whether it’s in North Korea or in Iran, then we have a better chance at better outcomes.

speaker: OBAMA
text: When President Bush decided we’re not going to talk to Iran, we’re not going to talk to North Korea, you know what happened?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Iran went from zero centrifuges to develop nuclear weapons to 4,000.

speaker: OBAMA
text: North Korea quadrupled its nuclear capability.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to try to have talks, understanding that we’re not taking military options off the table.

speaker: BROKAW
text: All right, gentlemen, we’ve come to the last question.

speaker: BROKAW
text: And you’ll both be interested to know this comes from the Internet and it’s from a state that you’re strongly contesting, both of you.

speaker: BROKAW
text: It’s from Peggy in Amherst, New Hampshire.

speaker: BROKAW
text: And it has a certain Zen-like quality, I’ll give you a fair warning.

speaker: BROKAW
text: She says, “What don’t you know and how will you learn it?

speaker: BROKAW
text: ” Senator Obama, you get first crack at that.

speaker: OBAMA
text: My wife, Michelle, is there and she could give you a much longer list than I do.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And most of the time, I learn it by asking her.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But, look, the nature of the challenges that we’re going to face are immense and one of the things that we know about the presidency is that it’s never the challenges that you expect.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s the challenges that you don’t that end up consuming most of your time.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But here’s what I do know.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I know that I wouldn’t be standing here if it weren’t for the fact that this country gave me opportunity.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I came from very modest means.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I had a single mom and my grandparents raised me and it was because of the help of scholarships and my grandmother scrimping on things that she might have wanted to purchase and my mom, at one point, getting food stamps in order for us to put food on the table.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Despite all that, I was able to go to the best schools on earth and I was able to succeed in a way that I could not have succeeded anywhere else in this country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The same is true for Michelle and I’m sure the same is true for a lot of you.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And the question in this election is: are we going to pass on that same American dream to the next generation?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Over the last eight years, we’ve seen that dream diminish.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Wages and incomes have gone down.

speaker: OBAMA
text: People have lost their health care or are going bankrupt because they get sick.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got young people who have got the grades and the will and the drive to go to college, but they just don’t have the money.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we can’t expect that if we do the same things that we’ve been doing over the last eight years, that somehow we are going to have a different outcome.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We need fundamental change.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s what’s at stake in this election.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s the reason I decided to run for president, and I’m hopeful that all of you are prepared to continue this extraordinary journey that we call America.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But we’re going to have to have the courage and the sacrifice, the nerve to move in a new direction.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Thank you.

speaker: OBAMA
text: BROKAW: Senator McCain, you get the last word.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Senator Obama had the opening.

speaker: OBAMA
text: You’re last up.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Well, thank you, Tom.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I think what I don’t know is what all of us don’t know, and that’s what’s going to happen both here at home and abroad.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: The challenges that we face are unprecedented.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Americans are hurting tonight in a way they have not in our generation.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: There are challenges around the world that are new and different and there will be different — we will be talking about countries sometime in the future that we hardly know where they are on the map, some Americans.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: So what I don’t know is what the unexpected will be.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: But I have spent my whole life serving this country.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I grew up in a family where my father was gone most of the time because he was at sea and doing our country’s business.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: My mother basically raised our family.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I know what it’s like in dark times.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I know what it’s like to have to fight to keep one’s hope going through difficult times.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I know what it’s like to rely on others for support and courage and love in tough times.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I know what it’s like to have your comrades reach out to you and your neighbors and your fellow citizens and pick you up and put you back in the fight.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: That’s what America’s all about.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I believe in this country.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I believe in its future.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: I believe in its greatness.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: It’s been my great honor to serve it for many, many years.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: And I’m asking the American people to give me another opportunity and I’ll rest on my record, but I’ll also tell you, when times are tough, we need a steady hand at the tiller and the great honor of my life was to always put my country first.

speaker: MCCAIN
text: Thank you, Tom.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Thank you very much, Senator McCain.

speaker: BROKAW
text: That concludes tonight’s debate from here in Nashville.

speaker: BROKAW
text: We want to thank our hosts here at Belmont University in Nashville and the Commission on Presidential Debates.

speaker: BROKAW
text: And you’re in my way of my script there, if you will move.

speaker: BROKAW
text: In addition to everything else, there is one more presidential debate on Wednesday, October 15, at Hofstra University in New York, moderated by my friend, Bob Schieffer of “CBS News.

speaker: BROKAW
text: ” Thank you, Senator McCain.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Thank you, Senator Obama.

speaker: BROKAW
text: Good night, everyone, from Nashville.

speaker: BROKAW
text: END Transcription by: CQ Transcriptions/Morningside
